$note: First dossier. Extracted 2026-08-23 from aether_gate/adapters/icom9700.py, adapters/icom/radios.py, and the gate's session history — see $source keys. Where the adapter and history disagree, history won and the code cite carries the note.

identity.$source: gate bring-up sessions 2026-06-30..07-16 on Nigel's IC-9700 (LAN)

usb_is_civ_only.$note: The 9700's USB has NO audio codec (bInterfaceClass 255, confirmed on the Pi) — USB is CI-V only; LAN is the ONLY audio path. Contrast IC-7300 (USB audio present).
usb_is_civ_only.$source: lsusb on Pi5, 2026-07-07 session (project memory: 'LAN AUDIO NOW WORKS')

single_client.$note: One RS-BA1 client at a time: a second session gets 'radio reports BUSY' and token renewals are rejected while another client holds the login.

remembers_peer_audio_port.$note: The radio keeps streaming audio to the PREVIOUS session's port after a client restart, ignoring the freshly advertised one. Consumers must bind FIXED local ports across restarts (gate uses civ=40410, audio=40411).

canReboot.$note: No remote reboot verb known for RS-BA1; AE's Icom backend also declines (over WiFi models, power-off is a one-way trip). Untested here.

capabilities.$tuningRanges_note: Region-neutral widest edges; band names use AE BandDefs vocabulary ('440', not '70cm'). Disjoint ranges — a single min/max envelope would falsely claim 148–420 MHz coverage.

txPowerBands.$note: Icom spec sheet says 75 W on 70cm; the gate's meter scaling currently uses 100 W for all non-23cm bands (icom9700.py _fwd_power_w band_max) — a known approximation to refine. hw evidence exists only for 2m.

second_receiver_readback.$note: RX2 freq/mode read reliably via the 07 B0 swap-read (cached at connect + on tune), NOT via 25 01 which is ambiguous. See receivers() ordering fix.

family_specific.$note: Icom CI-V wire vocabulary (schema rule 5: family facts live here, mirroring AE's IcomModel/IcomModelProfile split).

civ_address.$note: 0xA2 — the model default; user-changeable on the radio.

mode_bytes.$note: CI-V mode byte per native mode name (06/26 commands). FM-N is 0x12.

no_data_mode_byte.$note: The 9700 has NO distinct data-mode byte: DFM≡FM, DIGU≡USB on the rig — the 'data' part is purely the consumer's audio routing. Consumers with superset vocabularies (Flex) must fold to the base mode and echo the alias, or the radio→client sync snaps the display back.

consumer_fold.$note: Fold table for Flex-vocabulary consumers (from AE_MODE_ALIASES). An unmappable pick must be refused loudly, never silently dropped.

rf_power_level_semantics.$note: CI-V 14 0A returns 0–255 mapping to a 0–100% LEVEL of band max — NOT watts. First gate attempt converted %→fake watts; corrected. At the rig's 1% setting the raw read was 3 → level 1, while actual output measured ~0.78 W: the setting and the output are DIFFERENT quantities.

forward_power.$note: Standard Icom Po scale (0/50/100% at raw 0/143/213), interpolated; scale to band max watts. Spot-checked on hardware at the very low end: 1% setting → 15 11 read 0.73 W vs 0.78 W on the bench wattmeter (~6%). A full per-band bench cal would upgrade this to hw-measured.

poll_gating.$note: Polling Po while unkeyed is useless and wastes the CI-V budget; clear to 0 on unkey.

scope.$geometry_source: 618 consecutive frames decoded off this radio via RS-BA1, every one 475 px; bounds header cross-checked (centre 439.86406 MHz, 500 kHz span → 1052.6 Hz/px). AE-side measurement 2026-08-05.

keepalive.$note: The 9700 stops scope output without regular CI-V traffic; the gate's 10 Hz S-meter poll IS the scope keepalive (packet-capture derived).

stall_recovery.value: full session recycle (0x05 → are-you-there → login → conninfo), accepted in ~1 ms
stall_recovery.$note: When scope output stalls, in-session re-arm (27 10 01) and data-reopen do NOT restart it; only a fresh session does. ⚠ HISTORY: a '~2650-frame Icom firmware cap' was hypothesized and later REFUTED — SDR9700 sustained 179 pkt/s scope for 3m20s uninterrupted on the same radio; the stall signature was the gate port's own protocol drift. Recorded here so the refuted claim is never re-promoted to radio fact.

scope_frames_own_datagrams.$note: A scope datagram (FE FE E0 A2 27 00 00 …FD) contains raw amplitude bytes that routinely include stray FD / FE FE — generic CI-V frame-scanning INSIDE a scope datagram mis-decodes amplitude bytes as BCD frequency (the 'freq jumping around the band' bug). Detect 27 00 00, extract, and return; freq/mode/S-meter replies arrive in their own datagrams.

rx.$note: Requires its own RS-BA1 session on the audio port with the same are-you-there handshake; measured delivery 48192 samples/s (~+0.4%).

tx.$note: TX audio session needs txenable=1 in conninfo AND a valid remote_id from the are-you-there handshake — with remote_id=0 the radio silently REJECTS every TX-audio packet. Packet layout per SDR9700 audio_packet (ident 0x10 / sendseq 0x12 / datalen 0x16, frag 1364).

mode_set_needs_optimistic_echo.$note: After 06 <mode> the radio's next poll still reports the OLD mode briefly; a consumer that trusts the poll snaps the user's selection back. Set the local mirror optimistically on send.

initial_mode_needs_wait.$note: 26 00 reply lands asynchronously; reading immediately after connect seeds a default (USB) even when the rig is on FM. Wait for the real reply.

x-gate.$note: Aether-gate presentation & operator policy — NOT radio truth.
x-gate.$advertise_note: Costume: FLEX-6700 unlocks AE's native 2m band; 70cm/23cm ride AE's XVTR mapping.

tx_allowed_bands.$note: OPERATOR POLICY (Nigel): 23cm TX deliberately refused by the gate's key_tx guard — RX on 1.2 GHz is fine. A hard guard, not a remembered rule. Distinct from capabilities.txPowerBands, which states what the RADIO can do.

rf_power_read_only.$note: OPERATOR POLICY: AE's rfpower/tunepower sets stay unparsed; power is set at the rig.
